cards.back: The period of life spent in good functional health, defined by specified measures.
A biomarker intended to stand in for a clinical or functional outcome; it requires validation for that purpose.
A durable cell-cycle arrest state with context-dependent molecular and secretory features.
Senescence-associated secretory phenotype; a variable set of secreted factors, not a universal fixed signature.
The local and systemic environment that regulates stem-cell maintenance and function.
A method that follows descendants of defined cells over time to infer contribution and fate.
An event that prevents the outcome of interest from occurring or being observed, such as death before a functional endpoint.
Analysis that retains participants or experimental units in their assigned groups regardless of adherence, under a prespecified strategy.
An animal leaves observation for a reason other than the event; it counts as at risk until removal and is neither a death nor deleted.
ln 2 / G for a Gompertz hazard μ(t) = A·e^(G·t): the age interval over which the fitted hazard doubles.

cards.front: Why can survivor-only function comparisons mislead?
cards.back: If treatment changes who survives, survivor groups differ in composition, so differences mix treatment effects with selection by death.
A shorter late-life period of disability relative to lifespan; longer life does not guarantee it.
Platelets depend on BCL-xL to survive, so inhibiting it shortens platelet life span and lowers platelet counts.
Every randomized subject is analyzed in its assigned arm, with a prespecified rule for deaths and missing outcomes.
p16 promoter activity is not exclusive to senescent cells, and clearance is incomplete and differs by tissue.

cards.front: A useful role of senescent cells that clearance can remove
cards.back: In mouse wounds, senescent cells speed closure by secreting PDGF-AA; removing them delayed healing.
A blood-cancer-associated somatic mutation detected in blood, commonly at VAF of at least 2%, without a diagnosed hematologic cancer.

cards.front: Variant allele fraction to clone size
cards.back: For a heterozygous autosomal mutation without copy-number change, the fraction of mutant cells is about 2 × VAF.
Same-age pairs that receive the same joining surgery, separating partner-age effects from the procedure itself.

cards.front: What did the GDF11 debate teach?
cards.back: Reagents that also detected myostatin undermined the reported age decline; factor claims need specific assays and independent replication.
The residual of clock age after regressing it on chronological age in a reference population.

cards.front: How can a blood clock change without any cell changing?
cards.back: Clock estimates partly reflect cell-type proportions, so shifting composition moves the estimate.
OCT4, SOX2, KLF4 and c-MYC: factors that can reprogram somatic cells to pluripotency and erase their identity.

cards.front: Why is a larger clock decrease not always better?
cards.back: Past a threshold, reprogramming causes dedifferentiation and tumor risk, and pluripotent cells read as epigenetically young.
